paragraphs.text: If you want to know how to use Framer AI, the short answer is this: you describe the site in plain words, an AI agent builds real pages inside the Framer editor, and you keep editing them on the canvas before you publish. Framer's help center calls these Framer Agents, and it says everything the agent makes stays editable.

Framer describes Framer AI as the set of AI agents built into the product. An agent can start from a prompt or from a site you already have, and it can create pages, refine layouts, update CMS content or review SEO. It works on the real project, not on a separate mockup.

Framer's own AI website builder page lists four stages: start from a prompt, refine the design visually, add real site systems such as CMS content, SEO metadata, forms and analytics, then publish on Framer hosting and keep asking the agent for improvements.
How to use Framer AI to build your first site

paragraphs.title: 1. Create a new project
paragraphs.text: Sign up or log in, create a new project, then open the Agent tab in the right sidebar. A new chat opens with a field where you type your request.

paragraphs.title: 2. Write a specific first prompt
paragraphs.text: Say what the site is for, which sections it needs and what style you want. Framer's own example is a coffee roastery called Ember Roast with a hero, a section for three blends, testimonials and a contact section. The more concrete the first prompt, the less you fix later.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 1: A first draft you can work with
paragraphs.text: Build a one page website for [business name], a [what it does] in [city]. Sections: a hero with one clear headline and a button to [main action], [section 2], [section 3], customer testimonials, and a contact section with a form. Style: [two or three words, for example calm, warm, minimal]. Keep the copy short and plain.

paragraphs.title: 3. Refine it in the chat
paragraphs.text: Ask for one change at a time. Framer's examples are requests like making the hero full screen or adding a pricing section with three tiers. You can also select a layer or a section on the canvas first and ask the agent to change only that part.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 2: Fix one section, not the whole page
paragraphs.text: Change only the selected section: turn it into a vertical stack, make the headline shorter, and replace the image with the one I attached. Do not change any other section.

paragraphs.title: 4. Edit by hand on the canvas
paragraphs.text: The agent's pages are normal Framer pages. You can change text, layout, colors, images and spacing directly, the same way you would on a page you built yourself.

paragraphs.title: 5. Try big changes on a branch
paragraphs.text: Framer's guide describes an optional branch workflow: open the branch menu next to the project title, create a branch, let the agent work there, review the changes in the branch panel, then apply them to main and publish.

paragraphs.title: 6. Review, then publish
paragraphs.text: Before you publish, Framer's help center says to check the content, images, layout, links and how the pages behave on smaller screens. Then publish from Framer. The builder page says hosting includes SSL, CDN delivery and redirects.
What else the Framer agent can do

Framer's AI page shows the agent reviewing a site for low contrast, typos, missing alt text, SEO gaps and inconsistent styles. It also lists named skills such as design system, CMS content, removing AI-sounding writing and an SEO check, plus mentions with the @ key and references, where you upload images, files or links for the agent to use.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 3: A quick quality check before launch
paragraphs.text: Review this site before I publish. List every place with low text contrast, typos, images without alt text, missing page titles or descriptions, and buttons that do not link anywhere. Fix the typos and alt text, and show me the rest as a list.

Replace every placeholder. Framer's builder page calls the AI output a first draft and says teams should swap in real content and adjust layouts for different screen sizes. Fake testimonials and stock copy left on a live site do more harm than an empty section.
Framer AI free plan and pricing

Framer's builder page has a Get started for free button, so you can try the agent without paying first. The pages this guide used do not list the current plan limits, so check Framer's pricing page before you connect a custom domain or plan a site with heavy traffic.

For context, Popular Science reported in July 2023 that free Framer sites came with a Framer address and a small Framer badge, and that paid plans removed the free limits. That was the older Start with AI version of the tool, so treat those details as history, not as today's terms.
Where Framer AI falls short

The agent is fast at a first layout, but it does not know your business. It will happily write confident copy about services you do not offer, so read every line. It is also easy to burn time asking for vague changes. Short, specific requests aimed at one selected section work better than asking it to make the whole site better.
Keep a short brief in a note: your one line pitch, your three main sections, your colors and your tone. Paste it into new chats so every page sounds like the same site.
